name: STRATTEC SECURITY CORP

devils_advocate.strongest_counter: The gap that survives my base-year correction is not a mispricing, it is a disagreement about terminal multiple, and the market is the one with the evidence. This model discounts at 10.07% to a 2.5% perpetuity, which is roughly a 13x multiple on terminal free cash flow. Auto suppliers do not get 13x and never have. The reason is not sentiment: a mechanical access supplier to three North American OEMs faces vehicle architectures being redesigned around digital access, and every dollar of the gap I report comes from assuming a perpetuity that may not exist. Cancelled EV programmes have already cost Strattec real revenue — that is a live example of architecture change destroying content, flagged by management itself.
devils_advocate.what_would_prove_it: Content per vehicle on new programme awards, and the mix between legacy mechanical products and the power-access and electronic security lines. If new awards replace mechanical content one-for-one or better with electronic content, the perpetuity is safe and the multiple is wrong. If content shrinks per vehicle as architectures change, the market's implied decay is the honest number and the terminal value should not be there.
devils_advocate.already_visible: Ambiguous, and I have to say so again today because I could not resolve it. Cancelled EV programmes destroyed content, which is the bear mechanism in action. Against it, management says cancelled EV programmes are no longer an incremental headwind and is spending about $12M a year automating, which is not what you do to a business you expect to run off. The 10-K was filed on 2026-08-28 and would contain the programme-award and content-per-vehicle disclosure that settles this; SEC egress is blocked from this runtime and I could not open it. A second, weaker signal appeared today: the stock fell 6.5% intraday on no disclosure I could find, three days after the 10-K landed. That is consistent with someone reading the 10-K and disliking what is in it, and I cannot check.
devils_advocate.unresolved: The terminal multiple, which is the whole disagreement, unchanged from this morning. Also unchanged: I could not reconcile the $71.7M operating cash flow year against $18.7M of net income in the same year — a working-capital release of that size matters to what 'maintainable' means, and it is why I cut the base to $33M rather than trusting any single year. And there is still no dated catalyst; LESSONS is explicit that a small-cap value gap without an event that forces re-pricing is usually early, and this one has none. New today: I could not identify what caused the 6.5% intraday decline.

what_changed: Nothing about the business since this morning's pass; two items about the tape and the sell side. (1) Freedom Broker downgraded the stock in August 2026 on margin pressure, cutting estimates materially after the fiscal 2027 guidance. (2) The share price is $70.20 against $75.04 at this morning's 03:11 UTC screen — down 6.5% intraday on no company disclosure I could find. Restating the fiscal 2026 facts confirmed this morning's figures: record revenue of $579.4M, gross margin expanded 150 basis points to 16.5%, $46.3M of operating cash flow, $108.2M of cash and no debt at the 2026-06-28 year end, with the 10-K filed 2026-08-28. Fiscal 2027 guidance: North American production down about 2%, Ford/Stellantis/GM down nearly 6%, peso headwind about 100 basis points of gross margin.
consensus_case: The market pays auto-supplier multiples for auto suppliers, and Strattec is not an exception to that rule. At $70.20 the enterprise value is roughly $198M against about $50M of EBITDA — about 4x, squarely inside the 3.5-5x band the sector has traded in for a decade. The reason is not sentiment: the terminal value of a mechanical lock-and-latch supplier to three North American OEMs is genuinely uncertain, because vehicle architecture is being redesigned around digital access, and a supplier whose core product is a physical key has a real chance of not having a perpetuity at all. Fiscal 2027 makes that concrete: North American production is guided down about 2% overall and nearly 6% at Ford, Stellantis and GM specifically, and the Mexican peso at 16.90 against an 18.00 average last year costs roughly 100 basis points of gross margin. Freedom Broker cut its rating in August on exactly those margin pressures. Against a $52.0M reported FCFF base the price implies -25% annual decay; against the $33M base I think is maintainable it implies far less, but the market's point stands: it is pricing the possibility that there is no terminal value here, and that is a defensible thing to price.
base_case_rationale: I hold roughly -2% five-year FCFF growth off a $33M base, unchanged from this morning, because nothing I found today touches either input. Fiscal 2027 is a genuine down year — customer production off about 6% and a 100 basis point peso headwind — but the transformation is delivering measurably rather than aspirationally: gross margin up 150 basis points to 16.5% on 2.5% revenue growth, EBITDA up about 15%, and the stated 18-20% gross margin target on roughly $570-580M of revenue is worth $9-20M of incremental gross profit against a roughly $50M EBITDA base. A down year followed by a margin-led recovery averages out slightly negative. That is far below the naive +3.6% revenue CAGR, which mechanically applies top-line growth to a cash-flow base that has nothing to do with it. The $33M base, not the reported $52.0M, is the number that matters here and the reason is in the data-quality note.
key_risks: Terminal value is the whole gap — a mechanical access supplier may not have a perpetuity as vehicle architectures go digital
Customer concentration in GM, Ford and Stellantis, whose fiscal 2027 production is guided down about 6%
Peso strength worth roughly 100 basis points of gross margin, plus tariff costs that customer agreements push back onto the supplier
Operating cash flow has swung $12.3M / $71.7M / $46.3M across three years — 'maintainable' is a judgement, not a measurement
No dated catalyst, which by this project's own standing lesson usually means early
3.99M shares and $7.4M average daily dollar volume make this genuinely hard to own in size
A 6.5% intraday decline today that I could not attribute to any disclosure
watch_for: Progress toward the 18-20% gross margin target — the fiscal 2027 quarterly prints against 16.5%
New programme awards and content per vehicle, especially electronic versus mechanical mix
Whether fiscal 2027 capex stays near the guided $12M or steps up
Any use of the $108.2M cash pile — buyback, acquisition or dividend all reprice the equity differently
